subject: marbled crayfish
title: Millions of These Crayfish Exist, and Every One Is the Same Animal

scenes.text: Millions of these crayfish exist. They're all one animal.
The marbled crayfish. In 1995 one turned up in the German aquarium trade, sold as a Texas crayfish.
Then it laid eggs with no male. Every hatchling was female, and did the same. Clutches of up to 650.
In 2018 scientists sequenced their genomes. Animals from Germany and Madagascar differed by at most four mutations. One mother, around 1988.
Dumped in Madagascar, it spread from 1,000 to more than 100,000 square kilometers in ten years. Three researchers caught 150 by hand in one hour.
The only crayfish on Earth that clones itself. And it's winning.

description:
Every marbled crayfish on Earth is a clone of one animal that appeared in a German aquarium in 1995.
The species reproduces only by parthenogenesis: all individuals are female and lay unfertilised eggs, up to 650 at a time. A 2018 study in Nature Ecology and Evolution compared genomes from German aquariums and wild Madagascar populations and found no more than four differences between any two animals, tracing them to a single ancestor around 1988. In Madagascar its range grew about 100-fold between 2007 and 2017, to over 100,000 square kilometers.
Should a species that is one giant clone count as one animal or millions?
first_comment: The marbled crayfish is now banned from sale in the European Union. Which invasive species has surprised you the most?
